text: Done. GET /v1/datasets/{d}/releases/{r}/archive streams one accepted release, or a subset accepted as its own release, as a zip: one folder sanctity-DATASET-RELEASE with files and directories as released, including empty ones, and SHA256SUMS.txt beside it for shasum -a 256 -c. Entries are stored uncompressed, nothing is buffered, and the same release gives the same bytes in any server time zone. NativeRepository.readRelease supplies a reader that rechecks ReadContent on every 64 KiB, as readFile does. The zip index is written only after every file was read, so a download that loses access part-way fails with what was sent not a valid archive. Operator command: repository export PRINCIPAL DATASET RELEASE STORAGE NEW_DIRECTORY writes the release to a new directory and NEW_DIRECTORY.sha256 beside it, and refuses an existing destination. Criteria: 1 to 4 met. Criterion 5, throughput on a release of at least 5 GiB, was NOT measured here; it is carried by CORE3 with CORE4 as the remedy, and a note on CORE3 says so. The Download button belongs to SEE4 and SHARE1. Evidence: ReleaseArchiveSuite (3), ArchiveSuite on PostgreSQL (3, including a credential revoked on the first bytes), the packaged-service smoke test with a new export step, and scripts/check-postgres.sh (688 unit, 388 integration, crash and restore). Documented in docs/http-api.md, docs/http-api.openapi.json and docs/service-distribution.md.
